context.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and interoperability across international healthcare networks.

## Key Elements
- **Cross-Border Telehealth Platform**: Core system deployed on GCP (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`).
- **Patient**: End-user utilizing mobile and web clients.
- **Clinician**: Licensed medical professional conducting consultations and issuing prescriptions.
- **External Pharmacy Systems**: Receives e-prescriptions via regional protocols.
- **AI Model Provider / LLM API**: External service powering the symptom checker.
- **National Identity Providers**: External authentication systems using eIDAS and Login.gov.
- **National Health Registries**: Country-specific health data exchanges and US HIEs.

## Relationships
- **Patient -> Cross-Border Telehealth Platform (HTTPS/WebRTC)**: Video consultations, symptom checks, and consent management.
- **Clinician -> Cross-Border Telehealth Platform (HTTPS)**: Consultations and prescription authoring.
- **Cross-Border Telehealth Platform -> External Pharmacy Systems (REST/FHIR)**: E-prescription dispatch.
- **Cross-Border Telehealth Platform -> National Identity Providers (OIDC/SAML)**: User authentication and jurisdictional verification.
- **Cross-Border Telehealth Platform -> National Health Registries (REST/FHIR)**: Patient history and audit compliance.

## Technology Stack
- **GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`)**: Multi-region cloud infrastructure ensuring data residency constraints are met.
- **WebRTC**: Low-bandwidth video consultations supporting degraded modes below 300 kbit/s.
- **HL7 FHIR & National EU Standards**: Interoperability protocols for US health data and EU e-prescriptions.
- **OIDC/SAML**: Authentication protocols for cross-border trust federations (e.g., eIDAS).

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict regional data isolation to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA mandates while utilizing federated identity and standard interoperability protocols. The multi-region GCP deployment combined with robust WebRTC and FHIR integration ensures high availability, traceability for EU MDR, and reliable performance in low-bandwidth rural areas.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and resilience for unstable rural connections.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (Users)
- Web/Mobile Client SPA/PWA (Flutter/React)
- Google Cloud API Gateway (Entry point)
- Data Residency & Consent Router (Go)
- Core Services Backend (Go/Spring Boot)
- AI Symptom Checker Service (Python/FastAPI)
- Video Streaming Server (LiveKit WebRTC SFU on GKE)
- Interoperability Adapter (Node.js/TypeScript)
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL (Regional Data Storage)
- External Systems: Pharmacy Systems, LLM API, National ID Providers, Health Registries

## Relationships
- Patients/Clinicians to API Gateway via HTTPS/WSS
- API Gateway to Data Residency & Consent Router via gRPC
- Core Services to Cloud SQL via TCP/SQL
- Video Streaming Server to Clients via WebRTC over UDP/TCP
- AI Symptom Checker to External LLM API via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Enforces regional data isolation.
- Go: Used for Consent Router and Core Services for low latency and minimal footprint.
- Python/FastAPI: Powers the AI Symptom Checker for ML library compatibility.
- LiveKit (WebRTC SFU): Supports adaptive video streaming below 300 kbit/s.
- TypeScript: Powers Interoperability Adapter for FHIR/JSON manipulation.
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Stores partitioned regional transactional data.

## Rationale
Isolated regional GCP deployments and a dedicated Consent Router strictly enforce EU GDPR and US HIPAA data residency boundaries. Specialized WebRTC and interoperability adapters ensure low-bandwidth resilience and seamless cross-border regional health data integration.

Web/Mobile Client SPA/PWA.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It enforces strict regional data residency and regulatory compliance on Google Cloud Platform.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Patient, Clinician
- **External Systems**: External Pharmacy Systems, AI Model Provider / LLM API, National Identity Providers, National Health Registries
- **Containers**: Web/Mobile Client SPA/PWA, Google Cloud API Gateway, Data Residency & Consent Router, Core Services Backend, AI Symptom Checker Service, Video Streaming Server, Interoperability Adapter, Cloud SQL PostgreSQL
- **Components (Web/Mobile Client)**: UI Presentation Layer, State & Sync Manager, Secure Local Repository, WebRTC Media Client

## Relationships
- Patient / Clinician -> Web/Mobile Client SPA/PWA: Interacts via [HTTPS/WSS]
- Web/Mobile Client SPA/PWA -> Google Cloud API Gateway: Sends API requests via [HTTPS / REST & gRPC-Web]
- WebRTC Media Client -> Video Streaming Server (LiveKit SFU): Streams consultations via [WebRTC over UDP with TURN/STUN fallback]
- Data Residency & Consent Router -> Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Enforces region-locked persistence via [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol / TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- **Client**: Flutter & React (SPA/PWA) for multi-platform UI consistency and offline-first capabilities.
- **Local Storage**: Encrypted SQLite and IndexedDB using AES-256 via Web Crypto API for secure PHI/PII caching.
- **Video**: LiveKit WebRTC SFU on GKE with adaptive bitrate scaling for unstable connections (<300 kbit/s).
- **Cloud Provider**: Google Cloud Platform in regions `europe-west3` and `us-central1`.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict GDPR and HIPAA compliance by isolating regional data infrastructure while maintaining high availability and low-bandwidth resilience. Distributed microservices and client-side encryption meet rigorous healthcare security, traceability, and interoperability demands.

Google Cloud API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability across disparate regional networks.

## Key Elements
- **Web/Mobile Client SPA/PWA**: Patient and clinician interface built with Flutter/React supporting degraded network modes.
- **Google Cloud API Gateway**: Entry point containing internal components: API Router & Regional Dispatcher, Authentication & Authorization Filter, Rate Limiting & Resiliency Policy Enforcer, and Audit & Telemetry Logger.
- **Data Residency & Consent Router**: Go service managing regional data boundaries and explicit consent.
- **Video Streaming Server**: LiveKit WebRTC SFU deployed on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).
- **AI Symptom Checker Service**: Python/FastAPI service with versioned traceability logging.

## Relationships
- Web/Mobile Client SPA/PWA -> Google Cloud API Gateway: Sends API requests and video streams [HTTPS/WSS]
- API Router & Regional Dispatcher -> Authentication & Authorization Filter: Validates tokens [Internal gRPC]
- API Router & Regional Dispatcher -> Data Residency & Consent Router: Forwards regional payloads [gRPC]
- API Router & Regional Dispatcher -> Audit & Telemetry Logger: Streams request metadata [Cloud Pub/Sub / gRPC]

## Technology Stack
- **Google Cloud Platform (GCP)**: Cloud provider utilizing `europe-west3` and `us-central1` regions for strict data residency.
- **Google Cloud API Gateway**: Manages ingress traffic using Envoy-powered extensions.
- **LiveKit WebRTC SFU**: Powers video consultations on GKE for low-bandwidth environments.
- **PostgreSQL / Cloud SQL**: Regional data storage ensuring separation of EU and US health records.
- **HL7 FHIR & National Standards**: Interoperability protocols for US and EU e-prescriptions.

## Rationale
This architecture enforces GDPR and HIPAA compliance by isolating EU and US health data within designated GCP regions using intelligent API routing. It guarantees high availability and traceability for medical AI outputs even under unstable rural network conditions.

Data Residency & Consent Router.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. The system enforces strict regional data residency and GDPR/HIPAA compliance while supporting low-bandwidth connections.

## Key Elements
- **Patient & Clinician**: End users accessing the platform via Web/Mobile Client SPA/PWA (Flutter/React).
- **Google Cloud API Gateway**: Entry point for inbound client requests.
- **Data Residency & Consent Router**: Go-based container containing Geo-Routing Policy Engine, Consent Interceptor Middleware, Audit Logger, and Regional Proxy Dispatcher.
- **Core Services Backend**: Go/Spring Boot container managing business logic in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`.
- **AI Symptom Checker Service**: Python/FastAPI container for triage recommendations.
- **Video Streaming Server**: LiveKit WebRTC SFU on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).
- **Cloud SQL PostgreSQL**: Regional database instances.
- **External Systems**: National Identity Providers, National Health Registries, External Pharmacy Systems, AI Model Provider API.

## Relationships
- **Patient/Clinician** -> **Google Cloud API Gateway**: Sends HTTPS/WSS requests.
- **Google Cloud API Gateway** -> **Data Residency & Consent Router**: Routes inbound requests [gRPC].
- **Geo-Routing Policy Engine** -> **Consent Interceptor Middleware**: Passes validated regional context [In-memory Go struct].
- **Consent Interceptor Middleware** -> **Regional Proxy Dispatcher**: Triggers inter-region dispatch upon verified consent [In-memory].
- **Regional Proxy Dispatcher** -> **Core Services Backend**: Forwards requests to region-pinned instances [mTLS via gRPC].
- **Consent Interceptor Middleware** -> **Cloud SQL PostgreSQL**: Queries regional consent state [pgx / gRPC].
- **Core Services Backend** -> **AI Symptom Checker Service**: Evaluates symptom urgency [REST/gRPC].
- **Core Services Backend** -> **External Pharmacy Systems**: Sends e-prescriptions via national EU standards and US HL7 FHIR.

## Technology Stack
- **Google Cloud Platform (GCP)**: Targeted cloud provider using `europe-west3` and `us-central1` regions for regional data residency.
- **Go**: Language for API gateway, core backend, and Data Residency & Consent Router due to high throughput and low latency.
- **Python / FastAPI**: Framework for AI Symptom Checker Service to integrate ML libraries.
- **LiveKit (WebRTC SFU)**: Powers real-time video consultations supporting degraded modes below 300 kbit/s.
- **PostgreSQL (Cloud SQL)**: Relational data store isolated per region.
- **gRPC / mTLS**: Protocol for secure, high-performance inter-service communication.

## Rationale
This architecture uses GCP multi-region deployment (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`) combined with a dedicated Data Residency & Consent Router to strictly isolate EU and US health data per GDPR and HIPAA mandates. Go and gRPC provide the low latency and security required for real-time compliance enforcement without degrading video consultation performance.

Core Services Backend.analysis:
## Overview
The Core Services Backend is a Go-based microservice responsible for orchestrating consultations, prescriptions, and audit logs while enforcing regional data residency and consent policies. It processes healthcare operations securely for patients and clinicians across EU and US deployments.

## Key Elements
- Patient & Clinician Management Component (Go, Gin/Fiber)
- Consultation Coordinator Component (Go)
- Prescription Management Component (Go)
- Audit & Traceability Component (Go)
- Region-Aware Data Router Component (Go)
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL (GCP Database)
- Interoperability Adapter (Node.js/TypeScript)

## Relationships
- Consultation Coordinator -> Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Persists booking states [TCP/SQL]
- Prescription Management -> Interoperability Adapter: Dispatches prescription payloads [gRPC]
- Audit & Traceability -> Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Writes tamper-evident audit trails [TCP/SQL]
- Patient & Clinician Management, Consultation Coordinator, Prescription Management -> Region-Aware Data Router: Delegates persistence operations [In-process Go interface]
- Region-Aware Data Router -> Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Executes region-isolated transactional queries [TCP/SQL]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for optimal concurrency, performance, and fast startup times
- Gin/Fiber: High-performance HTTP micro-frameworks for routing and profile management

- gRPC: Efficient inter-service communication protocol for prescription routing
- TCP/SQL: Standard database connection protocol for transactional data persistence

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict GDPR and HIPAA compliance by routing queries regionally and filtering data based on patient consent. The modular Go-based component structure enables high availability and precise audit logging for medical traceability.

AI Symptom Checker Service.analysis:
## Overview
The AI Symptom Checker Service provides traceable, region-compliant symptom analysis and care urgency recommendations for patients in the EU and US. It decomposes into internal Python components deployed on GCP to meet strict healthcare regulations.

## Key Elements
* API Router & Validator (Python/FastAPI)
* Region-Aware Orchestrator (Python)
* Audit & Traceability Logger (Python / SQLAlchemy)
* LLM Integration Client (Python/HTTPX)
* AI Model Provider / LLM API (External System)
* Cloud SQL PostgreSQL (Database)

## Relationships
* API Router & Validator to Region-Aware Orchestrator: In-memory function call with Pydantic models
* Region-Aware Orchestrator to LLM Integration Client: Asynchronous method call
* LLM Integration Client to AI Model Provider / LLM API: HTTPS / REST with TLS 1.3
* Region-Aware Orchestrator to Audit & Traceability Logger: Local asynchronous event emission
* Audit & Traceability Logger to Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: SQLAlchemy / SQL over secure TCP

## Technology Stack
* Python / FastAPI: High-performance framework for rapid API routing and payload validation
* Pydantic: Strict data schema validation ensuring compliance with healthcare data formats
* HTTPX: Asynchronous HTTP client providing robust LLM API communication with circuit breakers
* SQLAlchemy: ORM for secure, structured writes to regional relational databases
* Structured Logging: Captures immutable audit trails for MDR and HIPAA compliance

## Rationale
This component architecture ensures EU MDR, GDPR, and HIPAA compliance by isolating regional data routing, enforcing strict payload minimization, and maintaining immutable audit logs for every symptom-checker interaction. Asynchronous processing and circuit breakers ensure high availability and resilience across distributed GCP regions.

Video Streaming Server.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and low-bandwidth resilience.

## Key Elements
- Web/Mobile Client SPA/PWA (Flutter/React)
- Google Cloud API Gateway
- Video Streaming Server (LiveKit WebRTC SFU on GKE) containing Signaling Component, SFU Media Router, Recording & Audit Sidecar, and Media Policy & Token Enforcer
- Data Residency & Consent Router (Go)
- Core Services Backend (Go/Spring Boot)
- AI Symptom Checker Service (Python/FastAPI)
- Interoperability Adapter (Node.js/TypeScript)
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL

## Relationships
- Web/Mobile Client SPA/PWA -> Google Cloud API Gateway: Sends API requests [HTTPS/REST]
- Signaling Component -> Media Policy & Token Enforcer: Validates regional access tokens [In-memory function call]
- Media Policy & Token Enforcer -> Data Residency & Consent Router: Verifies patient consent state [gRPC over TLS]
- Signaling Component -> SFU Media Router: Configures media tracks [Internal gRPC]
- SFU Media Router -> Web/Mobile Client SPA/PWA: Transmits adaptive media streams [WebRTC over UDP/ICE/DTLS]

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP regions `europe-west3` and `us-central1`): Enforces regional data residency constraints.
- LiveKit WebRTC SFU on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): Powers real-time video consultations with adaptive streaming.
- Go, Python (FastAPI), Node.js, and TypeScript: Backend component languages chosen for high performance and concurrency.
- PostgreSQL (Cloud SQL): Relational storage for platform metadata and application data.

## Rationale
This architecture isolates regional data traffic within GCP regions to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA compliance mandates. The decomposed video streaming components ensure low-bandwidth resilience for rural patients while strictly enforcing regional access policies.

Interoperability Adapter.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It enforces strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and localized interoperability.

## Key Elements
- **Patient & Clinician**: End users accessing the platform via Web/Mobile SPA/PWA.
- **Google Cloud API Gateway**: Manages ingress traffic.
- **Data Residency & Consent Router**: Go-based service routing data per region.
- **Core Services Backend**: Go/Spring Boot application managing core business logic.
- **AI Symptom Checker Service**: Python/FastAPI medical device supporting trace logging.
- **Video Streaming Server**: LiveKit WebRTC SFU on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).
- **Interoperability Adapter**: Node.js/TypeScript container decomposed into:
  - **Regional Routing Enforcer** (TypeScript)
  - **FHIR Translation Engine** (TypeScript/HAPI FHIR JS)
  - **EU National Standard Transformer** (TypeScript)
  - **Outbound Integration Dispatcher** (TypeScript/Axios)
- **Cloud SQL PostgreSQL**: Regional database instances.
- **External Systems**: External Pharmacy Systems, National Health Registries, National Identity Providers, AI Model Provider API.

## Relationships
- Core Services Backend -> Regional Routing Enforcer: Sends canonical health records with region tags [gRPC]
- Regional Routing Enforcer -> FHIR Translation Engine / EU National Standard Transformer: Routes payloads based on jurisdiction [In-memory]
- FHIR Translation Engine -> Outbound Integration Dispatcher: Passes validated US FHIR resources [In-memory]
- EU National Standard Transformer -> Outbound Integration Dispatcher: Passes localized EU payloads [In-memory]
- Outbound Integration Dispatcher -> External Pharmacy Systems / National Health Registries: Dispatches payloads [HTTPS/Mutual TLS, REST/FHIR]
- Web/Mobile Client -> Google Cloud API Gateway -> Data Residency & Consent Router -> Core Services Backend [HTTPS/gRPC]

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Provider**: Google Cloud Platform (GCP regions `europe-west3` and `us-central1`) for regional data isolation.
- **Backend & Adapters**: Go, Spring Boot, Python (FastAPI), Node.js, and TypeScript.
- **Frontend**: Flutter and React for Web/Mobile SPA/PWA.
- **Streaming**: LiveKit WebRTC SFU on GKE for resilient low-bandwidth video.
- **Database & Protocols**: Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, gRPC for internal service communication, HTTPS with mTLS for external integrations, and HL7 FHIR for US interoperability.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees GDPR and HIPAA compliance by isolating EU and US data processing within dedicated GCP regions using a Regional Routing Enforcer. Decoupling regional schema transformations from egress handling ensures reliable, compliant data exchanges with external pharmacies and health registries.

Cloud SQL PostgreSQL.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability across unstable rural networks.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (Users)
- External Pharmacy Systems, AI Model Provider, National Identity Providers, National Health Registries (External Systems)
- Web/Mobile Client SPA/PWA (Flutter/React)
- Google Cloud API Gateway (GCP API Gateway)
- Data Residency & Consent Router (Go)
- Core Services Backend (Go/Spring Boot)
- AI Symptom Checker Service (Python/FastAPI)
- Video Streaming Server (LiveKit WebRTC SFU on GKE)
- Interoperability Adapter (Node.js/TypeScript)
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL (PostgreSQL 15), containing:
  - Regional Database Instances (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`)
  - Database Schema & Partitioning Layer (PostgreSQL Row-Level Security)
  - Audit Logging Extension (`pgAudit`)
  - Connection Pooling & Encryption Component (Cloud SQL Auth Proxy & GCP Cloud KMS)

## Relationships
- Core Services Backend -> Connection Pooling & Encryption Component: Routes queries via [TCP/PostgreSQL over IAM-authenticated Unix sockets / TLS 1.3]
- Connection Pooling & Encryption Component -> Regional Database Instances: Forwards authenticated queries to regional databases
- Core Services Backend -> Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Persists and queries regional transactional health data via [TCP/SQL, TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Target cloud provider across `europe-west3` and `us-central1` regions for data residency compliance
- PostgreSQL 15 & Cloud SQL: Relational data storage with Row-Level Security (RLS) for tenant isolation
- `pgAudit`: Database extension for comprehensive logging to satisfy AI traceability and accountability (R-07)
- Cloud SQL Auth Proxy & GCP Cloud KMS: Secure connection management and Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) for data privacy

## Rationale
This architecture enforces strict regional data isolation to comply with GDPR and HIPAA mandates. The component-level database design guarantees auditability, encryption, and secure routing for cross-border healthcare data.
